clue.text: A bit like this leading Tory …

parts.note: so can mean in this way, like this
a side that is up is ahead, leading
CON is the abbreviation for Conservative, a Tory

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician leads in a small way, the ellipsis carrying the thought on into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis only links this clue's surface to 5 Across; it plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from French, the word means a tiny trace or slight amount of something.

clue.text: Players ultimately plump for Australian beer

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter is taken

parts.note: tubby means plump

explanation.surface: Team members choose a drink from down under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plump for' reads as 'choose', but 'plump' is the synonym and 'for' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australia a small squat bottle of beer, or the beer in it, has this name.

clue.text: At university, accept one may be quick on this

definitions.text: one may be quick on this

parts.note: being up means in residence at university
to take is to accept

explanation.surface: A student accepting a place, quick to grasp things.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the idiom of a person being quick to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone 'quick on' it understands things fast; the word means comprehension or absorption.

clue.text: New headline seen in cold Republican light

indicators.note: seen in places the rearranged letters within the other two

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: new means made afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fresh newspaper headline about a cold-hearted Republican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light' is a noun, a lamp, not the adjective the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an ornate hanging light fitting with branches for several bulbs.

clue.text: Part of church accepting one is innocent

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: the nave is the main body of a church
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A church space welcoming a blameless person.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe someone lacking worldly experience, unsophisticated and guileless.

clue.text: … demanding information during leave

indicators.note: during puts the information within the period of leaving, so one goes inside the other

parts.note: to exit is to leave
GEN is informal British slang for information

explanation.surface: Someone is pressing for details while trying to depart, continuing the Tory of the previous clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a situation or person that presses hard and requires much effort or attention.

clue.text: Thoughtful after former partner is costing too much

indicators.note: after puts the thoughtful piece behind the former partner

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
pensive means thoughtful

explanation.surface: Someone reflecting after a break-up finds it a pricey business.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something with a high, perhaps excessive, price.

clue.text: Keen on dope, with time for France

indicators.note: time stands for France, replacing it

parts.note: dope is slang for information, info
F is the international code for France

explanation.surface: A drug enthusiast who swaps time in France for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dope' is not a drug here but slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Being enthusiastic about something is informally being really into it.

clue.text: The average person from Spain — exceedingly male!

parts.note: E is the international code for Spain
very means exceedingly
a man is a male

explanation.surface: An ordinary Spaniard, described as extremely macho.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordinary or typical person is personified by this name from the medieval morality play.

clue.text: Section of quartet here dutifully tied to the spot

indicators.note: Section of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A string quartet loyally staying put in one place.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fastened by a rope to a fixed post is bound to that spot.

clue.text: Extremist cults pray, having lost all protection

indicators.note: each word sheds its outer letters, the protective covering around its middle

explanation.surface: Cult members praying without any safeguards, a picture of fanaticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having lost all protection' strips the first and last letters from both 'cults' and 'pray', leaving ULT and RA.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is someone holding extreme views, especially in politics or religion; an extremist.

clue.text: One minute — case of doctor being in a hurry

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
a doctor's case is a patient being treated

explanation.surface: Someone at the surgery saying 'one minute' while hurrying the doctor along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' looks like a container here, but it means a medical case, a patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Being restless and unwilling to wait is to be eager and in a rush.

clue.text: Food offered by divorcing hotheads?

parts.note: split hotheads into hot and heads: hot is baked, heads are beans in slang, giving a tinned food

explanation.surface: Quarrelling couples separating, hot-tempered and serving up a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divorcing' splits 'hotheads' into two words: hot means baked, and 'bean' is slang for a head, so hot heads become this food.
explanation.definitionFit: Haricot beans baked in tomato sauce, sold tinned, are a staple British food.

clue.text: Regularly play free instrument

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words that follow

explanation.surface: An invitation to play music at no charge on a regular basis.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small stringed harp of ancient Greece, a musical instrument.

clue.text: A series on hospital department will be caustic

parts.note: a string is a series of things
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A TV drama set in a hospital ward turns out biting.
explanation.definitionFit: A sharp, severe remark is described both ways; both mean harshly cutting.

clue.text: Free advice lands a source of riches

indicators.note: free signals the letters are released and arranged anew

explanation.surface: Getting advice at no cost brings in wealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' looks like 'at no cost', but it is the anagram signal on ADVICE LANDS A.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Arabian Nights tale, the hero finds a cave full of treasure, so the phrase means a store of riches.

clue.text: Stress aid designed for accidents

indicators.note: designed means put together in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tool to relieve stress made for people who've had mishaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are sudden calamitous events causing damage or harm.

clue.text: Made progress with cash up front on date

parts.note: an advance is money paid ahead of time

explanation.surface: Someone progressing after being paid early before a deadline.
explanation.definitionFit: To have moved forward or gone ahead is to have made progress.

clue.text: A forced entry may be in vain, so planned

indicators.note: planned means arranged, so the letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A break-in that was carefully plotted yet futile.
explanation.definitionFit: An army entering a country by force carries out this hostile incursion.

clue.text: Party approaches must protect important fringes of society for ages

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: the approaching word must wrap round and guard the other pieces

parts.note: nears means approaches
key means important

indicators.note: fringes are the outer edges, here the first and last letters

explanation.surface: Partygoers approaching must shield society's key fringe figures over a long period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link: the definition is just 'ages', in the sense of a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal British idiom means a very long time, as does ages.

clue.text: Restaurant in pub is trouble

indicators.note: in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Trouble breaks out at a pub with an eatery.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small, informal, often French-style restaurant.

clue.text: Shocked seeing husband in range shot heartlessly

indicators.note: in places the husband within the range

parts.note: an Aga is a British brand of range cooker

indicators.note: heartlessly means losing the middle letters of the word

parts.note: a shot as in a gunshot, the word itself

explanation.surface: A husband shot dead at the stove leaves everyone appalled.
explanation.walkthrough: An AGA is a heavy British kitchen stove. 'heartlessly' strips HO from the middle of SHOT, leaving ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Being filled with horror and amazement is being shocked.

clue.text: A military force retreating at a distance

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: the RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force

explanation.surface: A military force pulling back, keeping its distance.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean far off, some way away.

clue.text: Staggering time taken by a measurement of depth

indicators.note: taken by means received into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a sounding is a measurement of water depth

explanation.surface: Taking a depth reading took an amazing amount of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something so surprising it leaves one stunned.

clue.text: Ring exercises — oddly real drama

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O
PE is physical education, exercises

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters

explanation.surface: Boxing ring exercises turn into genuine theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: This musical stage work is a form of sung drama.

clue.text: One might bite in indignation

indicators.note: in says the answer lies within the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone snapping in anger at a perceived slight.
explanation.definitionFit: A small biting fly is an example of something that may bite.

clue.text: Customers may see legal right in court with team cut by half

indicators.note: in places the legal right within the court

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

indicators.note: cut by half keeps only the first half of the word

parts.note: a cricket or football side is an eleven

explanation.surface: Clients consult a lawyer about a legal claim in court involving a reduced team.
explanation.walkthrough: A cricket or football team is an eleven, the number of players; 'may see' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A business's clientele is its body of clients or regular customers.

clue.text: Actor surplus to requirements

definitions.meaning: a film actor in a non-speaking crowd role

explanation.surface: An actor told he is no longer needed.
explanation.definitionFit: One word is a background film performer and also means additional or more than needed.

clue.text: Means of attack editor backed

indicators.note: backed means turned back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: to set on someone is to attack them

explanation.surface: An editor supports a method of assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Means' is a verb here, not a noun; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To signify or indicate something is what a word or symbol does when it means it.

clue.text: Represents performances that are cancelled?

parts.note: acts are performances on stage
out can mean called off or cancelled

explanation.surface: A theatre rep describing shows that have been called off.
explanation.definitionFit: To dramatise or mime a story is to perform it physically, depicting it.
